section_summaries.individual_presentation: gradually progressive, severe walking difficulties; marked stiffness of the right leg with extension posturing and consecutive gait impairment with difficulties turning; leg stiffness immediately disappeared when sitting; extensor spasms of the legs provoked by plantar touching; hyperhidrosis; no exaggerated startle response, bradykinesia, tremor, or apraxia
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: high titers of GAD antibodies; exaggerated exteroceptive reflexes; continuous motor unit activity (CMUA); tumor screening was negative
section_summaries.individual_outcome: He had a good treatment response to diazepam and tizanidine and remained stable for 12 years he noticed a worsening of his symptom, which responded well on treatment with a corticosteroid pulse and oral tapering No new symptoms have developed during the follow-up of 13 years

section_summaries.individual_presentation: persistent pain and swelling of the left first metatarsophalangeal joint; progressive gait disturbance; stiffness starting in the left foot spreading over months to entire leg; painful leg spasms precipitated by unexpected noise or touch; reduced facial expression; mildly slow repetitive finger movements worse on the left without fatiguing; marked stiffness of the legs more pronounced on the left; striatal toe on the left; hyper-reflexia involved both legs no weakness; gait was slow and asymmetric, principally resulting from stiffness and posturing of the left leg with excessive knee extension and plantar flexion mainly on attempting to walk; overall posture was flexed rather than lordotic painful spasms
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: high titers of serum GAD antibodies, CMUA, and enhanced exteroceptive reflexes; MRI brain scan was normal apart from possible mild focal bilateral superior parietal atrophy diagnoses of SPS supported by electrophysiological and serological findings
section_summaries.individual_treatment: painful spasms responded to intravenous diazepam and immunotherapy (intravenous immunoglobulin, pulse prednisone, followed by weaning doses of oral prednisone) treatment response supports diagnosis
section_summaries.individual_outcome: On a follow-up of 16 years, stiffness remains well controlled; he has become disabled by psoriatic arthritis; he has not developed parkinsonism clinical course on long-term follow-up supports diagnosis
